title: Mother in grace (Lumen Gentium 62)
hookLine: Mary's motherhood continues without taking anything from Christ
tomorrow: what does a church owe a flood on the news?

cards: A friend walks past a statue of Mary with roses piled at her feet and asks, half joking: isn't that a bit much? Can she really be a mother to people without taking something from Christ?
It's a fair question, and Catholics ask it among themselves too. Two honest instincts pull on it.
Lumen Gentium gives both a voice, in one paragraph near the end of the document, and then draws a line they both have to keep.

teach.b: The first voice, at its best: Mary's motherhood didn't end in Bethlehem.
Paragraph sixty-two says it began with her yes at the Annunciation, "Behold the handmaid of the Lord," held without wavering all the way to the cross. And it continues.
Taken up into heaven, she keeps caring, by her prayers, for her Son's brothers and sisters still on the road. The paragraph even lists titles the Church gives her: Advocate, Helper, Mediatrix.
The second voice, at its best: careful.
Scripture says there is "one mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus." Every title for Mary has to fit inside that sentence, or it's too much. Now the council's line.
All of Mary's role, it says, neither takes anything away from nor adds anything to the dignity and power of Christ, the one mediator. No creature could ever be counted equal to the Word made flesh.

Then a picture: Christ's one priesthood is shared in different ways, and God's one goodness shines through many creatures. In the same way, one mediation gives rise to cooperation that draws everything from him.
A few paragraphs later the council names both mistakes to avoid: exaggeration, and narrow-mindedness.
Christians differ here. Catholics and Orthodox ask Mary's prayers; some other Christians pray to God directly and don't.

how: Catholics ask Mary's prayers in the Hail Mary, the rosary and other devotions, and the Church teaches that her role always depends on Christ, the one mediator.

Mary's ongoing care for believers, drawn from Christ

games.q: at your parish, one friend wants a bigger Marian procession every month; another worries it will crowd out Christ. from Lumen Gentium, what can both agree on?
o: honoring Mary can never go too far, so go bigger.
honor her, as long as all of it points back to Christ.
Marian devotion should quietly be dropped for safety.
games.why: the council warns against exaggeration and against narrow-mindedness, and sets one guardrail both voices share: her role takes nothing from Christ, the one mediator.

practice: Find an image of a mother nearby: a photo, a holy card, or one held in your mind. Look at it until you notice something new, the hands, the eyes, where she's looking.
If you pray, you can say slowly: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

wordCard.voice: Mother in grace. Mary's care for believers, which the council says flows from Christ and takes nothing from him.

orig.note: Latin title for Mary in Lumen Gentium 62, always understood under Christ the one mediator.

carryVoice: Keep this one: she takes nothing from him, and every honor she's given points back to her Son. Talk soon.
